verdict.rationale: Gmail's native Filters feature lets users define rules matching sender, subject, size, etc. that automatically trigger actions like labeling, archiving, or forwarding (gmail-docs-15, gmail-docs-28, gmail-docs-18), and the Gmail API's push notifications allow developers to build event-driven automations on mailbox changes (gmail-docs-3, gmail-docs-21, gmail-docs-27). However, these are simple field-matching rules, not flexible AI-native conditional logic, and no evidence shows integration with AI agents or complex multi-condition/action workflows beyond basic filters. Missing for 10: evidence of AI-driven or complex conditional rule logic, cross-service triggers, and any AI-native automation framework beyond basic filters/push API.
